nodes.name: Every 15 Minutes
nodes.notes: docs/workflows.md has WF-02 calling this on completion. It polls instead: PostgreSQL is the queue (docs/architecture.md), and a scoring failure must not be able to fail a research run.

parameters.query:
-- Claim researched companies and open their scoring run in one statement.
--
-- companies has no 'scoring' status, and inventing one would mean a migration
-- for a transient state. The agent_runs row IS the claim: a company with a
-- scoring run still 'running' is skipped. The 15 minute window means a run that
-- died without WF-99 closing it does not block the company forever.
--
-- FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on top of that, so two overlapping schedules take
-- different companies rather than the same one.
WITH claimed AS (
    SELECT c.id
    FROM companies c
    WHERE c.status = 'researched'
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM agent_runs r
          WHERE r.company_id = c.id
            AND r.agent_name = 'scoring'
            AND r.status     = 'running'
            AND r.started_at > now() - interval '15 minutes'
      )
    ORDER BY c.created_at
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'batch_size')::int
    FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
opened AS (
    INSERT INTO agent_runs (agent_name, company_id, input, status, model, started_at)
    SELECT 'scoring', claimed.id, $1::jsonb -> 'input', 'running', $1::jsonb ->> 'model', now()
    FROM claimed
    RETURNING id AS agent_run_id, company_id
)
SELECT o.agent_run_id,
       c.id AS company_id,
       c.name,
       c.domain::text AS domain,
       c.industry,
       c.employee_count,
       c.description,
       c.tech_stack,
       c.hiring_signals,
       -- The suppression trigger on outreach is the real guard; this is so
       -- scoring does not spend a model call on a company that can never be
       -- contacted.
       is_suppressed(('x@' || c.domain)::citext) AS domain_suppressed,
       COALESCE((
           SELECT (r.output #>> '{analysis,confidence}')::numeric
           FROM agent_runs r
           WHERE r.company_id = c.id AND r.agent_name = 'research' AND r.status = 'success'
           ORDER BY r.finished_at DESC NULLS LAST
           LIMIT 1
       ), 0) AS research_confidence,
       -- The research agent already chose an offer and WF-02 validated it against
       -- the enum. Asking the scoring model for it again only adds a way to be
       -- wrong, so it is carried through instead.
       (
           SELECT r.output #>> '{analysis,recommended_service}'
           FROM agent_runs r
           WHERE r.company_id = c.id AND r.agent_name = 'research' AND r.status = 'success'
           ORDER BY r.finished_at DESC NULLS LAST
           LIMIT 1
       ) AS research_offer,
       COALESCE((
           SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
                      'signal_type', s.signal_type, 'signal', s.signal,
                      'source_url', s.source_url, 'confidence', s.confidence)
                  ORDER BY s.created_at)
           FROM signals s WHERE s.company_id = c.id
       ), '[]'::json) AS signals,
       COALESCE((
           SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
                      'person_id', p.id, 'full_name', p.full_name, 'title', p.title,
                      'seniority', p.seniority, 'email', p.email::text,
                      'email_status', p.email_status))
           FROM people p WHERE p.company_id = c.id
       ), '[]'::json) AS people
FROM opened o
JOIN companies c ON c.id = o.company_id;

parameters.query:
-- Write the three component columns and, when there is someone to contact, the
-- lead. total_score and score_band are generated columns: the workflow must
-- never write them, so the band can never disagree with its own parts.
WITH payload AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS p
),
upd AS (
    UPDATE companies c
    SET fit_score            = (payload.p #>> '{scores,fit_score}')::smallint,
        research_score       = (payload.p #>> '{scores,research_score}')::smallint,
        decision_maker_score = (payload.p #>> '{scores,decision_maker_score}')::smallint,
        status               = payload.p #>> '{scores,company_status}'
    FROM payload
    WHERE c.id = (payload.p ->> 'company_id')::uuid
      AND c.status = 'researched'
    RETURNING c.id, c.total_score, c.score_band, c.status
),
ins AS (
    INSERT INTO leads (company_id, person_id, score, reason, recommended_offer, status)
    SELECT (payload.p ->> 'company_id')::uuid,
           (payload.p #>> '{lead,person_id}')::uuid,
           (payload.p #>> '{lead,score}')::smallint,
           payload.p #>> '{lead,reason}',
           payload.p #>> '{lead,recommended_offer}',
           payload.p #>> '{lead,status}'
    FROM payload
    WHERE payload.p -> 'lead' IS NOT NULL
      AND jsonb_typeof(payload.p -> 'lead') = 'object'
    ON CONFLICT (company_id, person_id) DO UPDATE
        SET score             = EXCLUDED.score,
            reason            = EXCLUDED.reason,
            recommended_offer = EXCLUDED.recommended_offer
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM upd)::int   AS companies_scored,
       (SELECT total_score FROM upd)     AS total_score,
       (SELECT score_band FROM upd)      AS score_band,
       (SELECT status FROM upd)          AS company_status,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM ins)::int   AS leads_written,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id'      AS agent_run_id;

nodes.notes: Writes the three components only. total_score and score_band are generated.

parameters.query:
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status        = 'success',
    output        = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
    error         = NULL,
    prompt_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,prompt_tokens}')::int,
    output_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,completion_tokens}')::int,
    finished_at   = now()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
RETURNING id, company_id, status, prompt_tokens, output_tokens, duration_ms;

parameters.query:
-- Close the run as failed and leave the company at 'researched' so the next
-- scheduled pass picks it up again. Scoring has nothing to roll back: it never
-- wrote a score.
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status      = 'error',
    error       = COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 'Scoring failed with no message'),
    output      = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
    finished_at = now()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
RETURNING id, company_id, status, error;

parameters.query:
-- docs/telegram.md lists "Company reaches HOT" as an immediate notification.
-- The band is read from the database, not from the model: score_band is a
-- generated column, so this fires on the score that was actually stored.
--
-- dedup_key is the company, with a long cooloff. A company that is re-scored
-- every night and stays HOT is not news twice.
WITH c AS (
    SELECT id, name, domain::text AS domain, total_score, score_band, status
    FROM companies
    WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'company_id')::uuid
      AND score_band = 'HOT'
),
detail AS (
    SELECT c.*,
           COALESCE((
               SELECT string_agg('- ' || s.signal ||
                                 COALESCE(' (' || s.source_url || ')', ''), E'\n'
                                 ORDER BY s.confidence DESC, s.created_at)
               FROM (SELECT * FROM signals WHERE company_id = c.id
                     ORDER BY confidence DESC, created_at LIMIT 5) s
           ), '(no signals on file)') AS signal_lines,
           (SELECT count(*) FROM people p WHERE p.company_id = c.id)::int AS people_count
    FROM c
)
SELECT q.notification_id, q.status, q.occurrences, q.deduplicated, detail.name, detail.total_score
FROM detail
CROSS JOIN LATERAL queue_notification(
    'company_hot',
    'company_hot:' || detail.id,
    'HOT: ' || detail.name || ' (' || detail.total_score || ')',
    detail.name || ' (' || detail.domain || ') scored ' || detail.total_score || ', band HOT.'
        || E'\n\nWhat got it there:\n' || detail.signal_lines
        || E'\n\n' || CASE WHEN detail.people_count = 0
                           THEN 'No contact on file yet, so no lead exists. WF-03 has to find one before anything can be sent.'
                           ELSE detail.people_count || ' contact(s) on file.' END,
    'immediate',
    jsonb_build_object('total_score', detail.total_score, 'score_band', detail.score_band,
                       'domain', detail.domain, 'people_count', detail.people_count),
    detail.id,
    NULL,
    make_interval(days => ($1::jsonb ->> 'cooloff_days')::int)
) q;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ company_id: $('Validate And Guard').item.json.company_id, cooloff_days: Number($env.HOT_ALERT_COOLOFF_DAYS || 30) } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- The nightly re-scoring sweep.
--
-- Scoring is not a one-off verdict. Two things make an old score wrong: a
-- contact appearing (WF-03 fills people, and decision_maker_score is a property
-- of that table, not a judgement - see docs/lead-scoring.md), and simple age.
--
-- This workflow does not re-score anything itself. It puts companies back to
-- 'researched' and the 15 minute pass above picks them up, so there is exactly
-- one scoring path and no second copy of the guards to keep in step.
--
-- IGNORE companies are left alone unless somebody was added to them. Re-scoring
-- a company that was capped to IGNORE spends a model call to reach the same
-- answer; a new contact is the one thing that can change it.
WITH candidates AS (
    SELECT c.id,
           c.score_band,
           COALESCE(ls.last_scored_at, c.updated_at) AS scored_at,
           (SELECT max(p.created_at) FROM people p WHERE p.company_id = c.id) AS newest_person_at
    FROM companies c
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT max(r.finished_at) AS last_scored_at
        FROM agent_runs r
        WHERE r.company_id = c.id
          AND r.agent_name = 'scoring'
          AND r.status     = 'success'
    ) ls ON true
    WHERE c.status = 'scored'
),
stale AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM candidates
    WHERE (newest_person_at IS NOT NULL AND newest_person_at > scored_at)
       OR (score_band <> 'IGNORE'
           AND scored_at < now() - make_interval(days => ($1::jsonb ->> 'max_age_days')::int))
    ORDER BY scored_at
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'batch_size')::int
),
requeued AS (
    UPDATE companies
    SET status = 'researched'
    WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM stale)
      -- Re-checked here so two overlapping sweeps cannot both requeue a row.
      AND status = 'scored'
    RETURNING id, name, domain::text AS domain, total_score, score_band
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS requeued,
       COALESCE(json_agg(json_build_object(
           'company_id', id, 'name', name, 'domain', domain,
           'previous_score', total_score, 'previous_band', score_band
       ) ORDER BY name), '[]'::json) AS companies
FROM requeued;
